protocol.weather_model: NCEP GFS Seamless via Open-Meteo Previous Runs API
protocol.fire_target: Any high-quality GOES FDCF detection in a fixed sector in a scan 24h after issue time; not ignition or route safety.
protocol.evaluation_unit: Sector-hour for fitting; route-sector-day (maximum score) for threshold selection and test reporting.
protocol.label_coverage_rule: Count a positive if any sampled pixel has a nominal/high-quality GOES fire label; count a negative only when at least 50% of the sector's fixed pixels have valid target labels. Require valid recent GOES history for at least 25% of fixed pixels.
protocol.training_period: 2024-01-01 through 2025-11-30 (only dates with GOES coverage and archived 24h weather)
protocol.threshold_rule: On validation only, maximize recall with route-sector-day precision >= 0.80 and at least 5 alerts; otherwise select no threshold.

precision_at_0_5_route_sector_day.caution: Nearby sectors and adjacent days can belong to one fire; this is not event-level precision.

persistence_gated_candidate.meaning: Continuation-risk filter only: issues a forecast alert only if satellite history at issue time already reports active fire in the sector; it does not predict ignition.

limitations: GOES fire detections are satellite labels, not ignition events or verified route-safety outcomes.
Eight point samples and coarse GFS grid do not represent full trail geometry.
Nearby sectors and adjacent days can belong to the same physical fire; route-sector-days are not independent incidents.
This comparison does not establish event-level precision because there is no exhaustive independent negative-event registry.
Class-weighted logistic scores are not calibrated probabilities.
